shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures firmed after a day of choppy trade on Wednesday on expectations that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would meet with his Chinese counterpart this weekend.

children: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures firmed after a day of choppy trade on Wednesday on expectations that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would meet with his Chinese counterpart this weekend.
Bessent on ​Tuesday said he would meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend ahead of a meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping next week.

Brazil's national crop agency Conab said the country's soybean production was expected to rise 0.7% to 181.64 million metric tons in 2026/27. But the planted area was seen expanding by the smallest percentage in two decades.
A Reuters poll of analysts expected the U.S. Department of Agriculture to report net export sales of soybeans on Thursday at 900,000-2,400,000 metric tons for the week ended Sept. 10.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) settled up 1-3/4 cents at $13.20-1/2 per bushel.
CBOT December soymeal (SMZ26) ended up $0.20 at $365.60 per ton.
fell 0.68 cent to finish at 69.67 cents per pound.
